datasets: BPD Arrests (Open Baltimore; reshaped extract as wb_records.csv)
Gun Offenders Registry (Open Baltimore; reshaped extract as 'gvt results.csv')
Safe Streets CY2024 mediations/events (MONSE PDF transcription; not Open Baltimore)
concurrency_primitives: 3 goroutines, one per CSV loader, each with a cap-1 result channel (concurrency.go:27-46); 3 goroutines counting per dataset into private maps via channels (analytics.go:30-78); sequential merge; no WaitGroup/Mutex/pool
design_patterns: None named; files split by role (revealer.go loaders, concurrency.go, analytics.go); normalizeNeighborhood join key
questions: How many unique neighborhoods appear across the datasets?
Which neighborhoods have both Arrest records and Gun Offender records?
Which neighborhood has the highest CVI mediations?
Which neighborhood has the fewest CVI community events?
Which neighborhoods have CVI activity but no Gun Offender records?
overview: Beginner Go program split into main/concurrency/revealer/analytics files: three goroutines load three CSVs fully into struct slices, three more count records per normalized neighborhood, and five questions are printed as plain text. Struct field names (OfficerName, SettlementAmount) contradict the actual gun-offender columns, there are no tests or flags, and the README is a first-person narrative. Canvas and direct_zip copies are identical except two README lines.
stakeholder_value: No stakeholder is named and the questions are trivial: a neighborhood count, a ~230-line list of neighborhoods present in both arrests and registry, a max/min over 10 Safe Streets sites, and a set difference whose sole answer ('park heights') is a naming artifact. MONSE or BPD would get no rates, rankings or actionable comparison from this output.
issues: Token concurrency (goroutine per file) and full in-memory loads; no streaming, pool, or concurrent join
Questions trivial; Q3/Q4 single-dataset; Q5 answer is a name-mismatch artifact; no stakeholder; no visualization
Data are reshaped/renamed extracts (synthetic RecordType/Count columns), not raw exports; third dataset hand-typed from a MONSE PDF; struct names contradict data
scripts/gen_mock.go is broken (decimal perm bits 1304) and would overwrite real data if it worked; not the default path
README narrative, claims make build runs the program, no macOS/verify section; go.mod go 1.27.2 forces toolchain download; direct_zip differs from Canvas only in README lines 19-21
rationale: Clean build and a fast end-to-end run on data verified (via Open Baltimore's live services) to derive from the real BPD Arrests and Gun Offenders Registry datasets earn build, most data, and run credit. Token concurrency, no memory design, misnamed structures without tests, trivial single-dataset or artifact-driven questions with no stakeholder or visualization, and a narrative README pull the total to 56/100 (F).
